verdicts.value: None on record
verdicts.why: The expansion is never said or shown on screen; the MCU wiki marks it as a conjectural name taken only from a tie-in book.

verdicts.value: A teenager the others call Teen frees Agatha Harkness from Wanda's spell and walks the Witches' Road with her.
verdicts.why: A sigil keeps anyone from learning his name, so the other characters refer to him as Teen; he does not name himself that.

verdicts.value: Nick Fury revives the Avengers Initiative when Loki steals the Tesseract, and puts Tony Stark, Steve Rogers, Bruce Banner, Thor and Natasha Romanoff on the Helicarrier together, where they argue more than they work. Then Loki's agents, led by a mind-controlled Clint Barton, attack the ship, and Loki kills Phil Coulson. Over New York they fight as a team, and Tony flies a nuke through the portal.
verdicts.why: Barton is under Loki's control from the start and is not among the arguing team; Loki's agents attack the Helicarrier while Loki, a prisoner, escapes after fatally wounding Coulson.

verdicts.value: Gorr, a man who lost his daughter and his faith, starts killing gods, and Jane returns as the Mighty Thor, wielding a reforged Mjolnir that is also hastening her death from cancer. They chase Gorr to Eternity, and Jane dies after joining the fight to save Thor. Gorr uses his wish to bring back his daughter and asks Thor to raise her. Thor becomes a father to a girl named Love.
verdicts.why: Gorr's wish would destroy the gods, not the universe; Jane joins the battle to save Thor, they destroy the Necrosword, and she then dies of her illness.

verdicts.value: Bruce: Empire State University, until the attack. Ross: a prisoner
verdicts.why: After Jean Grey turns him loose on Damage Control headquarters, Banner is removed from his post at Empire State University and sent to a psychiatric ward, so the plain last stage would not hold to the end.

verdicts.value: Fury grows suspicious of Project Insight, three helicarriers built to kill threats before they happen, and is shot by the Winter Soldier. He fakes his death, and Steve and Natasha uncover the truth: HYDRA has been growing inside S.H.I.E.L.D. since its founding, led by Alexander Pierce. They bring down the helicarriers, and Natasha leaks every S.H.I.E.L.D. secret online. S.H.I.E.L.D. is finished, and Fury goes underground.
verdicts.why: Steve and Natasha learn of HYDRA from Zola's preserved mind in the New Jersey bunker and work out that Pierce leads it; Fury only warns that S.H.I.E.L.D. is compromised and to trust no one.

verdicts.value: Fury grows suspicious of Project Insight, three helicarriers built to kill threats before they happen, and is shot by the Winter Soldier. He fakes his death, and Steve and Natasha uncover the truth: HYDRA has been growing inside S.H.I.E.L.D. since its founding, led by Alexander Pierce. They bring down the helicarriers, and Natasha leaks every S.H.I.E.L.D. secret online. S.H.I.E.L.D. is finished, and Fury goes underground.
verdicts.why: Steve and Natasha learn of HYDRA from Zola's preserved mind in the New Jersey bunker and work out that Pierce leads it; Fury only warns that S.H.I.E.L.D. is compromised and to trust no one.

verdicts.value: Years later, S.H.I.E.L.D. agent Phil Coulson keeps trying to set up a debriefing with Tony Stark after he escapes Afghanistan, and helps Pepper Potts expose Obadiah Stane. When Tony tells the world he's Iron Man, S.H.I.E.L.D.'s director, Nick Fury, is waiting in his living room to tell him he isn't the only superhero in the world, and that Fury is building something called the Avengers Initiative.
verdicts.why: The previous entry, Captain Marvel, is set in 1995 and Iron Man about thirteen years later, so 'decades later' is wrong.

verdicts.value: New stage at Agents of S.H.I.E.L.D. S6: "S.H.I.E.L.D.: Director Mackenzie. Coulson: dead"
verdicts.why: S6 opens a year after Coulson's death with S.H.I.E.L.D. rebuilding under Mack, and the death is revealed there, so the S5 'dying' stage cannot run through S6 and S7.

verdicts.value: Peter Quill, taken from Earth as a boy the night his mother died, steals an orb that Ronan the Accuser wants for Thanos. He's arrested on Xandar with Gamora, Thanos's adopted daughter, and bounty hunters Rocket and Groot, and they break out of prison with Drax, who lost his family to Ronan. The orb holds an Infinity Stone. When Ronan uses it to attack Xandar, Groot sacrifices himself to save them, and the other four hold the stone together and destroy him. Groot regrows as a sapling.
verdicts.why: Groot dies shielding the group when the Dark Aster crash-lands; Quill then holds the Stone with Gamora, Drax and Rocket sharing it to destroy Ronan.

verdicts.value: On TheDailyBugle.net, J. Jonah Jameson calls Spider-Man a fraud and Mysterio a hero, then airs the rest of Mysterio's video. Later, Betty Brant reports strange thunderstorms and sandstorms in New York, and the Bugle blames the Spider-Menace.
verdicts.why: Betty reports intense thunderstorms and sandstorms and wonders if supervillains are back; Electro and Sandman are never named, and naming them gives away No Way Home.
Peter says 'I'm Peter' and Ned answers 'Hello... Peter!', so Ned does say his name; the recap does not claim Ned remembers him.

verdicts.value: Bucky is a congressman now, investigating CIA director Valentina Allegra de Fontaine. When he finds her disposable assets, Yelena, John Walker and Ghost, he captures them to testify against her. When Bob becomes the Void, Bucky fights beside them, and Valentina announces them all as the New Avengers.
verdicts.why: Bucky captures the Thunderbolts and intends to have them testify in the impeachment proceedings against Valentina; he does not help them escape.

verdicts.value: Kamala fights beside her hero, Captain Marvel, and Monica Rambeau against Dar-Benn. Back on Earth, she visits Kate Bishop at her New York apartment and invites her to join a team of young heroes she's putting together.
verdicts.why: The film's locations put the visit at Kate Bishop's apartment in Manhattan; Jersey City appears only as the Khan home.

verdicts.value: Presumed dead, Frank tries to disappear into construction work. A hacker named Micro shows him the truth: his family died because of a CIA operation he served in, run by agent William Rawlins, and Frank's best friend, Billy Russo, was in on it. Frank kills Rawlins and leaves Russo's face scarred. The government clears him, and he walks free.
verdicts.why: Frank survived the explosion of the Blacksmith's ship and was reported dead; he did not stage it, and Micro is the one who fakes a death later.

verdicts.value: Eddie and Venom are on the run from the military and from Knull, the creator of the symbiotes, who hunts the key Venom carries. Venom sacrifices himself to save Eddie and destroy the key and the Xenophages, Knull's creatures, hunting them.
verdicts.why: The hunters are Knull's Xenophages; the other symbiotes fight on Eddie's side, and Venom leads the Xenophages into the acid tanks, sacrificing himself to destroy the Codex.

verdicts.value: Peter Quill, taken from Earth as a boy the night his mother died, steals an orb that Ronan the Accuser wants for Thanos. He's arrested with Gamora, Thanos's adopted daughter, and bounty hunters Rocket and Groot, and they escape prison with Drax, who lost his family to Ronan. The orb holds the Power Stone. When Ronan tries to use it to destroy Xandar, Peter, Gamora, Drax and Rocket hold the stone together and destroy him. Groot sacrifices himself and regrows as a sapling, and the five call themselves the Guardians of the Galaxy.
verdicts.why: Groot has already died shielding the group in the Dark Aster crash; only Quill, Gamora, Drax and Rocket hold the Stone to destroy Ronan.

verdicts.value: A terrorist called the Mandarin destroys Tony Stark's home while Tony, haunted by New York, can't sleep. Stranded in Tennessee with a broken suit, Tony learns the Mandarin is an actor, Trevor Slattery, hired by businessman Aldrich Killian to cover up the explosions of his Extremis soldiers. Tony and Rhodes stop Killian's plot, Rhodes rescues the President, and Pepper, who survived Extremis, kills Killian. Tony then has the shrapnel removed from his heart.
verdicts.why: On the tanker Rhodes takes the President to safety, Tony cannot save Pepper from her fall, and Pepper, kept alive by Extremis, kills Killian to save Tony.

verdicts.value: Before the class trip, Peter has a list of errands to finish, including his passport, and Spider-Man keeps getting in the way.
verdicts.why: Peter first buys a headphone adapter at the deli, then sells toys for MJ's necklace, and only then picks up his passport.

verdicts.value: On a school trip to Europe, Nick Fury, really the Skrull Talos in disguise, recruits Peter Parker to fight elemental monsters with Quentin Beck, and Peter, sure he isn't ready to replace Iron Man, gives Beck Tony's glasses. Beck is a former Stark employee whose monsters are illusions. Peter defeats him and starts dating MJ, until Beck's final video frames Spider-Man for his death and reveals Peter's identity.
verdicts.why: The same title reveals that the Fury seen throughout is the Skrull Talos in disguise, acting on the real Fury's orders while he is in space; real status, not what Peter believes.

verdicts.value: Jeffrey Mace is S.H.I.E.L.D.'s new director, and Coulson and Mack go looking for Daisy and find Robbie Reyes, a Ghost Rider. Holden Radcliffe's android, Aida, reads a book of dark magic called the Darkhold, replaces agents with Life Model Decoys and traps the team in the Framework, a virtual world where HYDRA rules. Mace dies, the team escapes, and Coulson, who has made a deal to be the Ghost Rider for a moment, burns away Aida, now a living woman. Then the team is taken, and Coulson wakes up on a space station.
verdicts.why: Mace is crushed in the Framework saving a student, and his real body dies too, while the team is still trapped; they escape the Framework later.

verdicts.value: Bullseye kills Foggy Nelson, and Matt Murdock gives up the mask. A year later, Wilson Fisk is elected mayor and builds a task force to wipe out vigilantes, with corrupt police wearing the Punisher's skull. Matt is pulled back in and puts the mask back on. When Fisk puts the city under martial law, Matt starts gathering allies.
verdicts.why: Matt suits up again in the middle of the run to rescue Angela from Muse, long before martial law, which comes only at the end, when he recruits Cherry, Kim and honest police. The fix only needs to move the mask, not add the Muse detail.

verdicts.value: while his father David, who experimented on himself years ago and passed the change on to his son, turns himself into something worse.
verdicts.why: Ross forbids human experimentation, so David experiments on himself and Bruce inherits the mutated DNA at birth.

verdicts.value: ["Four worlds, lost", "The Death of the Incredible Hulk"]
verdicts.why: The chapter's own recaps mark Earth-400005 terminated only at The Death of the Incredible Hulk; Returns and Trial are still set in that living world, so four lost is not true until then.

verdicts.value: ["Seven worlds, lost", "Captain America II: Death Too Soon"]
verdicts.why: The chapter's own recaps mark Earth-600043 terminated only at Captain America II: Death Too Soon, the second title set in that world.

verdicts.value: ["Nine worlds, lost", "The Incredible Hulk (1982)"]
verdicts.why: The chapter's own recaps mark Earth-8107 terminated only at The Incredible Hulk (1982); Spider-Man and His Amazing Friends is still set there.

verdicts.value: ["Seventeen worlds, lost", "The Incredible Hulk (1996)"]
verdicts.why: The chapter's own recaps mark Earth-534834 terminated only at The Incredible Hulk (1996); Fantastic Four (1994) is still set there.
